role: Enshrined as Tenjin (主祭神), the kami of scholarship.
regional_lore: Slandered and exiled from the court to Dazaifu, Michizane died here in 903. A series of plagues and lightning strikes on the capital were attributed to his vengeful spirit, who was pacified and enshrined as Tenman-Tenjin; over time the storm-god of grievance became the gentle patron of learning.

role: Principal Inari deity (主祭神); grain kami venerated for harvest and commerce.
Principal deity (主祭神) of the Hikawa network.
Consort enshrined with Susanoo; venerated here for matchmaking.
Descendant of Susanoo; deity of nation-building and good relationships.
Principal deity (主祭神); kami of nation-building and of binding relationships.
regional_lore: At Izumo, Okuninushi is honored as the builder of the land who ceded it to the heavenly grandchild (kuni-yuzuri) and withdrew into the unseen realm of relationships and fate; from this he became the great matchmaking kami, said to convene the assembled gods each autumn to decide the year's unions.

role: Enshrined sovereign (主祭神) of the Meiji era.
regional_lore: Enshrined here together with his consort in 1920, eight years after his death, by national subscription; the surrounding forest was raised from saplings donated from every province of Japan and the colonies.

role: Chief enshrined deity (主祭神); protector against plague and misfortune.
regional_lore: At Yasaka, Susanoo was long venerated in a fused identity with Gozu Tenno (牛頭天王), the Buddhist-derived deity of pestilence, until the 1868 separation restored his Shinto name. The Gion Matsuri originated as a goryo-e rite to appease him and quell epidemics.

role: Consort of Susanoo, enshrined alongside him.
